title: The free-energy principle: a unified brain theory?
relevance_summary: Supports the broad idea that perception, action, learning, and self-organization can be framed as free-energy minimization under generative models.
notes: Use as theoretical support, not as proof that the application implements biological FEP.

title: Whatever next? Predictive brains situated agents and the future of cognitive science
relevance_summary: Supports predictive-processing framing for hierarchical prediction, situated agents, action, attention, generative models, and prediction error.
notes: Use as conceptual support for predictive runtime metaphors and hierarchy, with limitations recorded per claim.

title: Canonical microcircuits for predictive coding
authors: Andre M. Bastos; W. Martin Usrey; Rick A. Adams; George R. Mangun; Pascal Fries; Karl J. Friston
relevance_summary: Supports predictive coding as a biologically grounded account involving cortical hierarchy, prediction, and prediction-error message passing.
notes: Good source when claims mention prediction-error style hierarchy; do not overstate as direct software equivalence.

title: A default mode of brain function
authors: M. E. Raichle; A. M. MacLeod; A. Z. Snyder; W. J. Powers; D. A. Gusnard; G. L. Shulman
publication: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
relevance_summary: Supports baseline/default-mode framing for internally organized brain activity and goal-directed modulation.
notes: Use for reflective/background state metaphors, not as evidence that any software module is conscious.

title: The attention system of the human brain
authors: Michael I. Posner; Steven E. Petersen
relevance_summary: Supports attention as a separable cognitive system with orienting, detecting, and executive aspects.
notes: Use for attention-boundary and perception-stage framing only.

title: Control of goal-directed and stimulus-driven attention in the brain
relevance_summary: Supports the distinction between goal-directed top-down attention and stimulus-driven salient-event detection.
notes: Useful for perception and attention-intake claims; avoid treating software salience rules as neural equivalence.

title: Computational modelling of visual attention
relevance_summary: Supports computational saliency-map framing for selecting relevant information under bottom-up and contextual influences.
notes: Use as computational inspiration for salience filtering, not as direct visual-system implementation proof.

title: An integrative theory of prefrontal cortex function
authors: Earl K. Miller; Jonathan D. Cohen
relevance_summary: Supports cognitive-control framing in which goal-relevant representations bias processing and behavior.
notes: Use for planning/executive-control analogy, not as proof of biological executive function.

title: Retrograde amnesia and memory consolidation: a neurobiological perspective
relevance_summary: Supports systems-consolidation framing for how memories can become reorganized over time.
notes: Use for consolidation metaphor and architecture support; app reflection is an engineered process.

title: The organization of recent and remote memories
relevance_summary: Supports recent-to-remote memory organization, reactivation, and system-level reorganization framing.
notes: Use for reflection/consolidation claims with clear non-biological limitations.

title: The memory function of sleep
relevance_summary: Supports offline memory consolidation and reorganization framing.
notes: Use for background reflection analogy only; the app does not model sleep physiology.

title: On the relationship between emotion and cognition
relevance_summary: Supports integrated emotion-cognition framing and cautions against overly isolated emotion versus cognition modules.
notes: Use for affective signal integration, not for claims of human emotion.

title: The somatic marker hypothesis and the possible functions of the prefrontal cortex
publication: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B
relevance_summary: Supports the idea that affective/body-state signals can bias reasoning and decision-making under uncertainty.
notes: Use as one hypothesis source and keep limitations explicit.

title: Parsing reward
authors: Kent C. Berridge; Terry E. Robinson
relevance_summary: Supports separating motivation, affect, learning, wanting, and liking in reward-related behavior.
notes: Use for motivation component framing, not for implementing reward circuitry.

title: Affective Neuroscience: The Foundations of Human and Animal Emotions
relevance_summary: Supports affective neuroscience framing in which emotional systems influence behavior and learning.
notes: Book source; use carefully and never as proof of machine feeling.

title: Meeting of minds: the medial frontal cortex and social cognition
authors: David M. Amodio; Chris D. Frith
relevance_summary: Supports social cognition framing involving self, others, action monitoring, and social inference.
notes: Use for role/social-posture analogies, not for claiming social cognition in the biological sense.

title: The neural basis of mentalizing
relevance_summary: Supports mentalizing and perspective-taking as social-cognition processes relevant to interaction stance.
notes: Use for role/perspective-taking framing with strict software limitations.

title: Social cognition and the human brain
relevance_summary: Supports broad social-cognition framing for interpreting others and guiding social behavior.
notes: Use as social-cognition support for role-selection metaphors, not as biological equivalence.

title: The magical number 4 in short-term memory: a reconsideration of mental storage capacity
relevance_summary: Supports limited short-term and working-memory capacity framing for keeping active context compact.
notes: Use for UI information-density rationale only; it does not prove a specific interface is usable.

title: The capacity of visual working memory for features and conjunctions
authors: Steven J. Luck; Edward K. Vogel
relevance_summary: Supports visual working-memory capacity limits for object-level visual information.
notes: Use for visual UI density and grouping rationale; not as proof of route behavior or accessibility.

title: Distracted and confused?: selective attention under load
relevance_summary: Supports attentional-load framing in which distractor processing depends on perceptual and cognitive load.
notes: Use for distraction/load-aware UI rationale; concrete usability still needs product tests or screenshot proof.
